sources.approval: Gallup, Presidential Job Approval Center (historical averages, highs and lows; Truman onward)
sources.debt: U.S. Treasury, Fiscal Data: Historical Debt Outstanding (fiscal year-end, nominal dollars)
sources.balance: FRED / U.S. OMB: Federal Surplus or Deficit as a percent of GDP, by fiscal year (1929 on)
sources.debtGdp: FRED / U.S. Treasury, BEA: Federal Debt as a percent of GDP, quarterly (1966 on)

presidents.name: George Washington
presidents.tagline: The general who agreed to give up power.
presidents.impact: Proved a republic could hand power over peacefully, and set the two-term custom that held for nearly a century and a half.
pros: Built the Cabinet and the executive branch from a blank page
Neutrality Proclamation kept the young nation out of Europe's wars
Hamilton's plan put the Revolution's debts on a repayment path
cons: Held enslaved people and signed the Fugitive Slave Act of 1793 (he freed those he owned in his will)
Led 13,000 militia against the Whiskey Rebellion
The Jay Treaty with Britain split the country

presidents.name: John Adams
presidents.tagline: Chose peace with France and paid for it politically.
presidents.impact: Ended the undeclared Quasi-War with France by negotiating, then accepted losing the 1800 election and handed power to his rival.
pros: Avoided a full war with France when his own party wanted one
Built up the Navy and created the Department of the Navy (1798)
Transferred power peacefully to the opposing party in 1801
cons: Signed the Alien and Sedition Acts, which jailed newspaper critics
New taxes sparked Fries's Rebellion in Pennsylvania
Feuded openly with Hamilton and split the Federalists

portrait.credit: Gilbert Stuart, c. 1800-1815 (National Gallery of Art)

presidents.name: Thomas Jefferson
presidents.tagline: Doubled the country with a single signature.
presidents.impact: The Louisiana Purchase (1803) roughly doubled U.S. territory and sent Lewis and Clark west.
pros: Louisiana Purchase for about $15 million
Sent the Lewis and Clark expedition
Cut spending and paid down the debt
cons: Enslaved more than 600 people over his life, including his own children
Embargo Act of 1807 wrecked trade and hurt farmers and merchants
Admitted he had no clear constitutional authority for the Purchase

world.t: Haiti wins independence; Napoleon crowns himself emperor

presidents.name: James Madison
presidents.tagline: The Constitution's architect, tested by war.
presidents.impact: The War of 1812: the capital burned, but the nation survived and came out more confident (the "Era of Good Feelings").
pros: Chief author of the Constitution and the Bill of Rights
Held the country together through a war it was not ready for
Chartered the Second Bank and a protective tariff in 1816
cons: Entered the war with a tiny army and weak finances
British forces burned Washington, D.C. in 1814
New England Federalists talked of secession at the Hartford Convention

world.t: Napoleon's army is destroyed in Russia
Waterloo; Mount Tambora erupts, causing 1816's "year without a summer"

presidents.name: James Monroe
presidents.tagline: Told Europe to stay out of the Americas.
presidents.impact: The Monroe Doctrine (1823) set a lasting rule of U.S. foreign policy, and the Missouri Compromise postponed the slavery crisis.
pros: Acquired Florida from Spain (1819)
Monroe Doctrine warned European powers away from the hemisphere
A calm, one-party stretch of national confidence
cons: The Missouri Compromise let slavery spread west of the Mississippi
The Panic of 1819 caused the nation's first big depression
Backed the American Colonization Society's removal schemes

world.t: Mexico wins independence; Greek revolt begins
Ayacucho ends Spanish rule in South America

presidents.name: John Quincy Adams
presidents.tagline: A brilliant diplomat with a Congress that said no.
presidents.impact: Proposed roads, canals, a national university and an observatory; Congress blocked most of it, but the vision shaped later "internal improvements."
pros: One of America's greatest diplomats, author of the Monroe Doctrine in practice
Pushed science, a national observatory and public works
Later a leading anti-slavery voice in the House
cons: Won the House vote of 1824 despite Jackson's popular plurality: the "corrupt bargain" charge
Opponents in Congress blocked his agenda
The 1828 "Tariff of Abominations" enraged the South

world.t: First public steam railway opens in England
Earliest surviving photograph taken in France

presidents.name: Andrew Jackson
presidents.tagline: Brought the common voter in, and pushed Native nations out.
presidents.impact: Opened politics to far more white men and strengthened the presidency, while the Indian Removal Act (1830) led to the Trail of Tears.
pros: Mass democracy: far more white men voted and ran for office
Faced down South Carolina in the Nullification Crisis to hold the Union together
The national debt was nearly paid off by 1835
cons: Indian Removal Act and the Trail of Tears
Held enslaved people and defended slavery
Killing the Second Bank and the Specie Circular helped set up the Panic of 1837

world.t: July Revolution in France; Belgium breaks away
Britain abolishes slavery across its empire

presidents.name: Martin Van Buren
presidents.tagline: Inherited a crash and took the blame.
presidents.impact: The Panic of 1837 and the long depression that followed defined his term and cost him reelection.
pros: Ten-hour workday for federal workers (1840)
Created an Independent Treasury to keep government money out of failing banks
Kept the peace in border crises with Britain and Canada
cons: Depression, bank failures and unemployment
The Trail of Tears removals were carried out on his watch (1838)
Seminole War dragged on at high cost

world.t: First Opium War begins; photography is announced
Treaty of Waitangi in New Zealand

presidents.name: William Henry Harrison
presidents.tagline: Thirty-one days.
presidents.impact: The first president to die in office. His death forced the country to decide what happens when a vice president takes over.
pros: The "Log Cabin" campaign of 1840 invented modern mass campaigning
Military hero of the Battle of Tippecanoe
cons: Gave the longest inaugural address, about two hours, in the cold
Barely governed before he died of illness
Earlier, as governor, pressured Native nations into land sales

world.t: Britain occupies Hong Kong Island in the Opium War
New Zealand becomes a British colony

presidents.name: John Tyler
presidents.tagline: "His Accidency" wrote the rule for succession.
presidents.impact: The Tyler Precedent: a vice president becomes the full president, not an acting one. He also annexed Texas.
pros: Set the succession precedent that held until the 25th Amendment
Webster-Ashburton Treaty settled the Maine border peacefully (1842)
Texas annexation resolution signed days before he left
cons: Vetoed his own party's bank bills; the Whigs expelled him
Annexing Texas expanded slavery and led to war with Mexico
Later served in the Confederate Congress

world.t: Treaty of Nanking ends the Opium War
Morse sends the first long-distance telegraph message

presidents.name: James K. Polk
presidents.tagline: Set four goals, hit all four, and left after one term.
presidents.impact: The Mexican-American War added California and the Southwest, about a third of today's lower 48 states.
pros: Oregon Treaty with Britain (1846) peacefully set the northern border
Gained California, Nevada, Utah and more
Founded the Naval Academy (1845) and signed the Smithsonian into law (1846)
cons: War began over a disputed border; Lincoln and Thoreau opposed it
New territory reignited the fight over slavery (Wilmot Proviso)
Enslaved people worked his plantation

world.t: Revolutions sweep Europe; Marx and Engels publish the Communist Manifesto
Gold found at Sutter's Mill, California

presidents.name: Zachary Taylor
presidents.tagline: A war hero who would not bend on the Union.
presidents.impact: Resisted southern threats of secession over California and the new territories. His sudden death left the crisis to his successor.
pros: Wanted California admitted directly as a free state
Warned he would lead the army against secessionists
Popular, straight-talking Mexican War hero
cons: Himself a slaveholder
Little legislation passed in sixteen months
Died suddenly, in the middle of the crisis

world.t: Russia helps crush the Hungarian Revolution
Taiping Rebellion begins in China, one of history's deadliest wars

presidents.name: Millard Fillmore
presidents.tagline: Signed the compromise that bought ten years.
presidents.impact: Signed the Compromise of 1850, including the harsh Fugitive Slave Act, delaying the Civil War but deepening the divide.
pros: The Compromise delayed civil war for a decade
Ordered the Perry expedition that opened Japan
Admitted California as a free state
cons: The Fugitive Slave Act forced citizens to help capture escapees
Enforcing it destroyed Whig support in the North
His party fractured and never won again

world.t: Napoleon III proclaims the Second French Empire

presidents.name: Franklin Pierce
presidents.tagline: The Kansas-Nebraska Act lit the fuse.
presidents.impact: The Kansas-Nebraska Act (1854) reopened slavery in the territories, sparked "Bleeding Kansas" and gave birth to the Republican Party.
pros: Gadsden Purchase completed the southern border (1853)
Perry's Treaty of Kanagawa (1854) opened Japan to trade
Kept the budget in surplus
cons: Kansas-Nebraska Act and the violence that followed
Ostend Manifesto hinted at seizing Cuba
Enforced the Fugitive Slave Act against northern protests

portrait.credit: Mathew Brady, restored by Adam Cuerden

presidents.name: James Buchanan
presidents.tagline: Watched the Union come apart.
presidents.impact: Seven states left the Union before Lincoln took office, and Buchanan declared secession illegal but did nothing to stop it. Historians often rank him among the worst presidents.
pros: First transatlantic telegraph messages exchanged with Queen Victoria (1858)
Minnesota and Oregon admitted as states
Experienced diplomat
cons: Pressured the Supreme Court toward the Dred Scott decision (1857)
Panic of 1857 and a weak response
Took no action as seven states seceded

world.t: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species

presidents.name: Abraham Lincoln
presidents.tagline: Held the Union together and ended slavery.
presidents.impact: Won the Civil War, issued the Emancipation Proclamation (1863) and pushed the Thirteenth Amendment through Congress before his assassination.
pros: Preserved the Union
Emancipation Proclamation and the Thirteenth Amendment
Homestead Act, Pacific Railway Act and land-grant colleges (Morrill Act)
cons: Suspended habeas corpus, jailing people without trial
Approved the execution of 38 Dakota men in 1862
The war killed roughly 620,000 to 750,000 soldiers

world.t: Russia frees its serfs; Kingdom of Italy proclaimed

presidents.name: Andrew Johnson
presidents.tagline: Impeached for fighting Congress over Reconstruction.
presidents.impact: His clash with Congress over Reconstruction ended in the first presidential impeachment (1868). The Senate acquitted him by one vote.
pros: Alaska Purchase (1867) for $7.2 million
Kept federal government functioning after Lincoln's assassination
Stayed loyal to the Union as a Southern senator
cons: Vetoed the Civil Rights Act of 1866 and the Freedmen's Bureau extension
Went easy on former Confederate leaders
Impeached in 1868

presidents.name: Ulysses S. Grant
presidents.tagline: Used federal power to protect Black citizens, until the country got tired.
presidents.impact: Enforced the Fifteenth Amendment and crushed the first Ku Klux Klan, though scandals and fatigue weakened Reconstruction.
pros: Enforcement Acts broke the first Klan
Created the Department of Justice (1870)
Established Yellowstone, the first national park (1872)
cons: Corruption scandals (Whiskey Ring, Credit Mobilier) in his administration
Panic of 1873 depression
Wars against Plains nations and the broken Black Hills treaty

presidents.name: Rutherford B. Hayes
presidents.tagline: Won a disputed election, then ended Reconstruction.
presidents.impact: Withdrew the last federal troops from the South in 1877 after the Compromise of 1877, ending Reconstruction.
pros: Began civil service reform
Honest administration after Grant's scandals
First White House telephone and typewriter
cons: Withdrawing troops left Black Southerners without federal protection
Sent troops against the Great Railroad Strike of 1877
Took office after the disputed 1876 election

world.t: Edison demonstrates a practical light bulb

presidents.name: James A. Garfield
presidents.tagline: Shot in July, gone by September.
presidents.impact: His assassination by a disappointed office seeker led directly to the Pendleton Civil Service Act (1883).
pros: Backed Black civil rights and public education
Took on the "spoils system" of political jobs
A self-made scholar and Civil War general
cons: Too short a term to accomplish much
Doctors' unsterile probing likely caused the infection that killed him

presidents.name: Chester A. Arthur
presidents.tagline: The machine politician who became a reformer.
presidents.impact: Signed the Pendleton Act (1883), creating a merit-based civil service that ended much of the spoils system.
pros: Pendleton Civil Service Act
Began rebuilding the Navy with steel ships
The Brooklyn Bridge opened in 1883
cons: Signed the Chinese Exclusion Act (1882)
Tariff of 1883 satisfied few
Hid a fatal kidney illness

presidents.name: Grover Cleveland
presidents.tagline: Reputation: honest. Habit: the veto pen.
presidents.impact: Signed the Interstate Commerce Act (1887), creating the first federal regulatory commission.
pros: Interstate Commerce Act, the first federal regulatory agency
Vetoed hundreds of fraudulent pension bills
Accepted the Statue of Liberty (1886)
cons: Signed the Dawes Act, which broke up Native communal lands
Little response to farmers' and workers' distress
Lost the 1888 electoral vote despite winning the popular vote

world.t: Congo Free State under Belgium's king
Benz patents the first gasoline automobile

presidents.name: Benjamin Harrison
presidents.tagline: The "Billion-Dollar Congress" and the first antitrust law.
presidents.impact: Signed the Sherman Antitrust Act (1890), the first federal law against monopolies.
pros: Sherman Antitrust Act
Six western states admitted in 1889-90
Modernized the Navy
cons: The McKinley Tariff raised prices and cost Republicans the 1890 midterms
Wounded Knee massacre in 1890
Lost the 1892 election

presidents.name: Grover Cleveland
presidents.tagline: The only president to serve two non-consecutive terms.
presidents.impact: The Panic of 1893 brought a deep depression, and his use of federal troops against the Pullman Strike (1894) divided the country.
pros: Repealed the Silver Purchase Act to protect the gold standard
Kept a firm line on honest government
Stood against annexing Hawaii by force
cons: Panic of 1893 depression and widespread unemployment
Sent troops to break the Pullman Strike
Lost his own party's support

world.t: Lumière brothers show the first films; Röntgen discovers X-rays

presidents.name: William McKinley
presidents.tagline: Made the U.S. an overseas power.
presidents.impact: The Spanish-American War (1898) gave the U.S. the Philippines, Guam and Puerto Rico. He was assassinated in 1901.
pros: Economic recovery and prosperity
Gold Standard Act of 1900
Quick victory in 1898
cons: Annexation of the Philippines led to a brutal war with Filipino independence fighters
Annexed Hawaii despite local opposition
Assassinated in Buffalo, 1901

world.t: Spain loses its last major colonies
Boer War begins in South Africa
Boxer Rebellion in China; Planck launches quantum theory

presidents.name: Theodore Roosevelt
presidents.tagline: Trust-buster, conservationist, canal-builder.
presidents.impact: Broke up powerful monopolies, protected about 230 million acres of public land and began the Panama Canal.
pros: Square Deal, Pure Food and Drug Act (1906)
Protected about 230 million acres of public land
Nobel Peace Prize (1906) for ending the Russo-Japanese War
cons: Backed Panama's break from Colombia to get the canal
Discharged 167 Black soldiers after the Brownsville incident, without a trial
"Big Stick" interventions in Latin America

presidents.name: William Howard Taft
presidents.tagline: Later became Chief Justice, the job he actually wanted.
presidents.impact: Sent the income-tax (16th) Amendment to the states and brought more antitrust cases than Roosevelt, but split his party.
pros: Filed more antitrust suits than Roosevelt did
Sixteenth Amendment sent to the states (1909)
Created the Department of Labor
cons: Payne-Aldrich Tariff angered reformers
Feud with Roosevelt split the Republicans in 1912
"Dollar Diplomacy" in Latin America

portrait.credit: Pach Brothers, restored by Adam Cuerden

presidents.name: Woodrow Wilson
presidents.tagline: Progressive reforms at home, "make the world safe for democracy" abroad.
presidents.impact: Led the U.S. through World War I, created the Federal Reserve and backed a League of Nations the Senate refused to join.
pros: Federal Reserve, Federal Trade Commission, income tax
19th Amendment passed Congress in 1919
Helped design the postwar order and the League of Nations idea
cons: Re-segregated parts of the federal workforce
Espionage and Sedition Acts jailed dissenters
Senate rejected the Treaty of Versailles; the 1918 flu killed about 675,000 Americans

world.t: Influenza pandemic kills tens of millions

presidents.name: Warren G. Harding
presidents.tagline: "A return to normalcy," then scandal.
presidents.impact: Teapot Dome and other scandals became public after he died in office, leaving a lasting image of cronyism.
pros: Washington Naval Conference limited battleships (1921-22)
Budget and Accounting Act created the federal budget process
Freed the jailed Socialist leader Eugene Debs (1921)
cons: Teapot Dome oil-lease scandal and Veterans' Bureau fraud
Appointed friends who betrayed him
Little progress on civil rights or lynching law

world.t: Mussolini marches on Rome; Soviet Union formed

presidents.name: Calvin Coolidge
presidents.tagline: The quietest president of the loudest decade.
presidents.impact: Small-government "Silent Cal" presided over the Roaring Twenties boom, with tax cuts and shrinking debt.
pros: Tax cuts and budget surpluses paid down debt
Signed the Indian Citizenship Act (1924)
Steady, honest after Harding
cons: Did little as stock speculation and farm distress grew
Immigration Act of 1924 set restrictive national quotas
Vetoed farm-relief bills twice

world.t: Lindbergh flies solo across the Atlantic

presidents.name: Herbert Hoover
presidents.tagline: A great humanitarian whose term met the Great Depression.
presidents.impact: The 1929 crash and the Great Depression defined his term; unemployment reached about 25 percent.
pros: Began the Hoover Dam
Created the Reconstruction Finance Corporation (1932)
Famed for feeding millions in Europe after WWI
cons: Smoot-Hawley Tariff deepened the global slump
Slow, limited federal relief
Army cleared the Bonus Army from Washington in 1932

presidents.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
presidents.tagline: The only president elected four times.
presidents.impact: The New Deal built the modern safety net (Social Security, FDIC), and he led the Allies through most of World War II.
pros: Social Security Act (1935), FDIC, SEC and rural electrification
Rallied the nation and the Allies in World War II
Lend-Lease and the Atlantic Charter
cons: Ordered the incarceration of about 120,000 Japanese Americans (1942)
1937 court-packing attempt
Unemployment stayed high until wartime spending

portrait.credit: Leon A. Perskie, 1944 (FDR Presidential Library), cropped and retouched

presidents.name: Harry S. Truman
presidents.tagline: "The buck stops here."
presidents.impact: Ended World War II, launched the Cold War framework (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO) and desegregated the armed forces.
pros: Marshall Plan helped rebuild Western Europe
Executive Order 9981 desegregated the military
Berlin Airlift and NATO
cons: Atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki remain debated
Korean War ended in stalemate
Loyalty investigations fed the Red Scare

presidents.name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
presidents.tagline: The general who warned about the military-industrial complex.
presidents.impact: The Interstate Highway System reshaped American life, and NASA was founded in response to Sputnik.
pros: Interstate Highway Act (1956)
Ended the Korean War
Sent federal troops to enforce school integration at Little Rock (1957)
cons: CIA-backed coups in Iran (1953) and Guatemala (1954)
Slow to push civil rights legislation
Let McCarthyism run before it collapsed; U-2 spy plane incident (1960)

presidents.name: John F. Kennedy
presidents.tagline: Youngest elected president; assassinated at 46.
presidents.impact: Steered the world away from nuclear war in the Cuban Missile Crisis and set the goal of a Moon landing.
pros: Cuban Missile Crisis resolved without war (1962)
Peace Corps and the Moon goal
Limited Nuclear Test Ban Treaty (1963)
cons: Bay of Pigs invasion failed (1961)
Increased U.S. advisers in Vietnam
Slow on civil rights until 1963

world.t: Berlin Wall built; Gagarin is first human in space

presidents.name: Lyndon B. Johnson
presidents.tagline: Signed the Civil Rights Act, and escalated Vietnam.
presidents.impact: The Civil Rights Act (1964), Voting Rights Act (1965), Medicare and Medicaid; also the Vietnam War's massive escalation.
pros: Civil Rights Act and Voting Rights Act
Medicare, Medicaid, Head Start, Higher Education Act
Great Society anti-poverty programs
cons: Vietnam escalation to over 500,000 troops, based partly on the disputed Gulf of Tonkin incident
Riots and protests at home
Chose not to run again in 1968

world.t: Six-Day War in the Middle East

presidents.name: Richard Nixon
presidents.tagline: Opened China, then resigned.
presidents.impact: Visited China (1972) and eased Cold War tension, created the EPA, and became the only president to resign, over Watergate.
pros: Opening to China (1972) and SALT I arms treaty
Created the EPA; signed the Clean Air Act
Brought U.S. troops home from Vietnam; ended the draft
cons: Watergate cover-up and resignation
Secret bombing of Cambodia
Wage and price controls, then inflation

world.t: Apollo 11 lands humans on the Moon
Yom Kippur War and oil embargo

presidents.name: Gerald Ford
presidents.tagline: Never elected as president or vice president.
presidents.impact: Calmed the country after Watergate, but his pardon of Nixon was deeply controversial and likely cost him in 1976.
pros: Restored a sense of calm and openness
Helsinki Accords (1975)
Signed the law that became IDEA, guaranteeing special education
cons: Pardon of Nixon
Recession and inflation
Saigon fell in 1975

world.t: Saigon falls; Khmer Rouge takes Cambodia

presidents.name: Jimmy Carter
presidents.tagline: Peace in the Middle East, trouble at home.
presidents.impact: Brokered the Camp David Accords between Egypt and Israel, but inflation and the Iran hostage crisis defined his term.
pros: Camp David Accords (1978)
Panama Canal treaties; created the Departments of Energy and Education
Put human rights at the center of foreign policy
cons: Stagflation: high inflation and unemployment together
Iran hostage crisis lasted 444 days
Gas lines and the energy crisis

world.t: Iranian Revolution; Soviet invasion of Afghanistan

presidents.name: Ronald Reagan
presidents.tagline: "The Great Communicator."
presidents.impact: Tax cuts and a defense buildup at home; at the end, arms-control talks with Gorbachev eased the Cold War.
pros: Inflation fell sharply
INF Treaty with the Soviets (1987)
Tax Reform Act of 1986
cons: Large deficits; federal debt roughly tripled
Iran-Contra affair
Slow federal response to the AIDS epidemic

world.t: Gorbachev takes power in the USSR
Reagan and Gorbachev sign the INF Treaty

presidents.name: George H. W. Bush
presidents.tagline: Managed the end of the Cold War.
presidents.impact: Guided the U.S. through the fall of the Berlin Wall and the Soviet breakup, and led the coalition in the Gulf War (1991).
pros: Americans with Disabilities Act (1990)
Gulf War coalition liberated Kuwait
Clean Air Act amendments of 1990
cons: Broke his "no new taxes" pledge in 1990
Recession of 1990-91
1989 invasion of Panama was criticized abroad

world.t: Berlin Wall falls; Tiananmen Square crackdown
World Wide Web opens to the public

presidents.name: Bill Clinton
presidents.tagline: Budget surpluses and the internet boom.
presidents.impact: The longest peacetime economic expansion in U.S. history; he was impeached in 1998 and acquitted in 1999.
pros: Federal budget surpluses in the late 1990s
About 22 million jobs created
NAFTA (1994) and welfare reform (1996)
cons: Impeached for lying under oath and obstruction (acquitted)
Little action to stop the Rwandan genocide
1994 crime bill and 1999 bank deregulation still debated

world.t: Rwandan genocide; Mandela elected in South Africa

presidents.name: George W. Bush
presidents.tagline: Presidency reshaped by September 11.
presidents.impact: The 9/11 attacks led to the War on Terror, wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, and a sweeping security buildup. The 2008 financial crisis ended his term.
pros: PEPFAR AIDS relief for Africa, credited with saving millions of lives
Unified the country after 9/11
No Child Left Behind and Medicare Part D
cons: Iraq War launched over weapons of mass destruction that were not found
2008 financial crisis and recession
Slow response to Hurricane Katrina; expanded surveillance

presidents.name: Barack Obama
presidents.tagline: First Black president.
presidents.impact: Led the recovery from the Great Recession, passed the Affordable Care Act (2010), and oversaw the raid that killed Osama bin Laden.
pros: Affordable Care Act extended insurance to roughly 20 million more people
Unemployment fell from about 10% to under 5%
Paris Climate Agreement (2015)
cons: Slow recovery for many families
Federal debt grew by several trillion dollars
Expanded drone strikes; red-line decision in Syria and the rise of ISIS

presidents.name: Donald Trump
presidents.tagline: First term: tax cuts, a pandemic and two impeachments.
presidents.impact: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (2017), three Supreme Court appointments, the COVID-19 pandemic and Operation Warp Speed, and two impeachments.
pros: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act; low unemployment before the pandemic
Operation Warp Speed produced vaccines in under a year
Abraham Accords and the First Step Act
cons: Impeached twice (2019, 2021); January 6 Capitol attack
Pandemic response debated; trade-war tariffs
Federal deficits grew even before COVID

presidents.name: Joe Biden
presidents.tagline: Took office at 78, then withdrew from the 2024 race.
presidents.impact: Signed the Infrastructure Law, the CHIPS and Science Act and the Inflation Reduction Act, amid high inflation and wars abroad.
pros: Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (2021)
CHIPS and Science Act (2022) boosted chip manufacturing
Unemployment stayed under 4% for long stretches
cons: Inflation peaked above 9% in 2022
Chaotic Afghanistan withdrawal (2021)
Record border encounters; age concerns led him to leave the 2024 race

presidents.name: Donald Trump
presidents.tagline: A second, non-consecutive term, still underway.
presidents.impact: The term is in progress. Historians have not yet judged it, and this card is a snapshot that may be out of date.
pros: Supporters cite the 2025 tax-and-spending law and sharply lower border crossings
Supporters cite tougher trade bargaining through tariffs
cons: Critics cite higher prices and trade tensions from tariffs
Critics cite the record 43-day government shutdown in late 2025
